summary_zh: 南印度圣公会圣公会新闻社表示，基督徒在圣诞节期间面临“不可接受的敌意”
title_zh: 南印度教会表示，基督徒在圣诞节期间面临“不可接受的敌意”
author: Anglican Communion News Service

title: UK leaders, hundreds gather to honor murdered Christian politician Ann Widdecombe
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham and four of his predecessors joined around 600 people at Westminster Cathedral on Thursday for a memorial service for Ann Widdecombe, the former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman who was found murdered in her home in July. She was 78.
summary_zh: 周四，安迪·伯纳姆（Andy Burnham）首相和他的四位前任与约600人一起在威斯敏斯特大教堂参加了安·威德康姆（Ann Widdecombe）的追悼会。安·威德康姆是前保守党大臣兼英国改革党发言人，今年7月在家中被谋杀，享年78岁。
title_zh: 英国政要和数百人齐聚一堂，悼念遇害的基督教政治家安·威德康姆
author: Christian Today

title: Christian social worker wins major court battle after losing job over biblical beliefs
summary: The Court of Appeal has ruled that a mental health charity unlawfully discriminated against a Christian social worker after discovering his opposition to same-sex marriage in online social media posts.
summary_zh: 上诉法院裁定，一家心理健康慈善机构在社交媒体帖子中发现一名基督教社工反对同性婚姻后，对其进行了非法歧视。
title_zh: 一名基督徒社工因圣经信仰而失去工作，但在重大法庭诉讼中胜诉
author: Christian Today

title: Spirit Embassy founder Uebert Angel offers apology to Zimbabwe’s president from jail
summary: Uebert Angel, a Zimbabwean presidential envoy and founder of the Spirit Embassy church, has apologized to President Emmerson Mnangagwa for statements made by "international prophets" that were widely seen as threats against the country's leadership over his arrest.
summary_zh: 津巴布韦总统特使兼Spirit Embassy教会创始人Uebert Angel就“国际先知”发表的言论向总统埃默森·姆南加古瓦（Emmerson Mnangagwa）道歉，这些言论被普遍视为针对该国领导层的威胁，原因是Uebert Angel被捕。
title_zh: 灵使馆创始人Uebert Angel在狱中向津巴布韦总统道歉
author: Leonardo Blair

title: Nearly 40% of Americans consider ministry as concerns over pastor shortage grow
summary: Nearly 40% of adults in a recent survey said they have considered a faith-based leadership role such as ministry, seminary or chaplaincy, but most have never taken a step toward pursuing it.
summary_zh: 在最近的一项调查中，近40%的成年人表示，他们曾考虑过担任基于信仰的领导职务，如牧师、神学院或随军牧师，但大多数人从未采取行动去追求这些目标。
title_zh: 随着对牧师短缺的担忧日益加剧，近 40% 的美国人考虑从事牧职
author: Ryan Foley

title: Evangelical activist implies God punished Charlie Kirk for 'turning' on Israel: 'It will be to your peril'
summary: Laurie Cardoza-Moore, a prominent Christian Zionist activist who hosts "Focus On Israel" on NRB TV, appeared to suggest during a recent interview that God allowed the late Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk to be assassinated because he was not adequately supporting Israel.
summary_zh: 劳里·卡多扎-摩尔（Laurie Cardoza-Moore）是一位著名的基督教犹太复国主义活动家，她在NRB电视台主持《聚焦以色列》（Focus On Israel）节目。在最近的一次采访中，她似乎暗示上帝允许已故的“转折点美国”（Turning Point USA）创始人查理·柯克（Charlie Kirk）被暗杀，因为他没有充分支持以色列。
title_zh: 福音派活动家暗示上帝惩罚查理·柯克“背叛”以色列：“这将危及你”
author: Jon Brown

title: Maine mother asks Supreme Court to review order barring her from taking daughter to church
summary: A Maine mother is asking the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene after the state's highest court upheld a custody order giving her daughter's father authority over whether the 13-year-old attends her mother's church and what religious materials she receives. Her lawyers say the order also bars the girl from being exposed to the Bible without the father's approval.
summary_zh: 在缅因州最高法院维持一项监护令后，一名缅因州母亲正请求美国最高法院介入。该监护令赋予其女儿的父亲决定权，决定这名13岁女孩是否参加母亲的教会活动以及她可以接收哪些宗教材料。她的律师表示，该裁定还禁止该女孩在未经父亲同意的情况下接触《圣经》。
title_zh: 缅因州母亲请求最高法院审查禁止她带女儿去教堂的命令
author: Samantha Kamman

title: Televangelist George Bloomer on $62.2M discrimination suit: ‘They believed me’
summary: Just over a month after winning a $62.2 million racial discrimination verdict against The Word Network and its owner, Kevin Adell, televangelist George Bloomer is breaking his silence about the legal fight, which he compares to the biblical story of David and Goliath.
summary_zh: 在赢得针对The Word Network及其所有者Kevin Adell的6220万美元种族歧视判决一个多月后，电视布道家George Bloomer打破了对这场法律斗争的沉默，他将这场斗争比作圣经中大卫与歌利亚的故事。
title_zh: 电视布道家乔治·布鲁默就6220万美元的歧视诉讼案表示：“他们相信我”
author: Leonardo Blair

title: 77 Thanksgivings later, 1 verse still shapes my prayers
summary: As a seminary student facing a personal disappointment, Richard Land read "In everything give thanks" and asked what he had to be thankful for. God answered with health, freedom to worship, a devoted wife and a church in which to preach.
summary_zh: 理查德·兰德（Richard Land）是一名神学院学生，正面临着个人挫折。他读到“凡事谢恩”，并问自己有什么值得感恩的。上帝的回答是：健康的身体、自由的崇拜、忠贞的妻子和可以布道的教会。
title_zh: 77个感恩节过去了，一节经文仍在塑造我的祷告
author: Richard D. Land

title: Ben & Jerry's sweet talk on abortion has a bitter aftertaste
summary: What does ice cream have to do with abortion? Absolutely nothing. That hasn't stopped Ben & Jerry's from churning out abortion activism, most recently through its "Into the Mix" podcast.
summary_zh: 冰淇淋与堕胎有什么关系？绝对没有任何关系。但这并没有阻止本与杰莉（Ben & Jerry's）大肆鼓吹堕胎运动，最近一次是通过其播客节目《Into the Mix》。
title_zh: Ben & Jerry's关于堕胎的甜言蜜语留下了苦涩的回味
author: Ryan Bomberger

title: 6 ways to build a legacy of generosity for your descendants
summary: A reader whose life was shaped by Larry Burkett's books asks how to leave a legacy of stewardship and generosity for their children and grandchildren. The answer begins with a simple truth: everything we own belongs to God.
summary_zh: 一位读者的生活深受拉里·伯基特（Larry Burkett）著作的影响，他想知道如何为自己的子孙后代留下管家精神和慷慨奉献的传承。答案始于一个简单的真理：我们所拥有的一切都属于神。
title_zh: 为后代建立慷慨遗产的6种方式
author: Chuck Bentley

title: Christian father of 3 killed by Muslims who threw him off boat 'like Jonah' for sharing the Gospel
summary: Muslims in Uganda threw a Christian father of three children off a water taxi into a lake after he shared the Gospel with passengers, causing him to drown.
summary_zh: 在乌干达，一名有三个孩子的基督徒父亲向水上出租车的乘客传福音，结果被穆斯林从船上扔进湖里，导致溺亡。
title_zh: 一名基督徒父亲因传福音而被穆斯林“像约拿一样”扔下船，惨遭杀害，留下3个孩子。
author: Morning Star News

title: Pakistan province backs tougher blasphemy laws critics say put Christians at risk
summary: Rights advocates criticized a resolution passed in the Punjab Provincial Assembly on Tuesday calling for harsher punishment for blasphemy against the wives, family members and companions of Islam’s prophet.
summary_zh: 周二，旁遮普省议会通过了一项决议，要求对亵渎伊斯兰先知的妻子、家人和同伴的行为施以更严厉的惩罚，人权倡导者对此表示批评。
title_zh: 巴基斯坦一个省份支持更加严厉的亵渎法，批评人士称该法使基督徒面临风险
author: Christian Daily International/Morning Star News

title: Over 139,000 sign petition opposing drag show mocking Nativity, depicting baby Jesus
summary: Over 100,000 people have signed a petition opposing a drag show in Hackney after promotional material depicted the baby Jesus wearing nipple tape.
summary_zh: 超过10万人签署了一份请愿书，反对在哈克尼举办一场变装秀，因为宣传材料中描绘了婴儿耶稣贴着乳贴。
title_zh: 超过13.9万人签署请愿书，反对模仿耶稣诞生的变装秀，其中有耶稣婴儿的形象。
author: Christian Today

title: Accreditor approves 20 programs for Olivet University after move to Missouri
summary: Olivet University has received approval from the Association for Biblical Higher Education for 20 new programs, from an English-language certificate to a doctorate in information technology, five months after the Christian school moved its main campus from California to Missouri.
summary_zh: 奥利韦特大学在将主校区从加利福尼亚州迁至密苏里州五个月后，获得了圣经高等教育协会对20个新专业的批准，这些专业涵盖从英语证书到信息技术博士学位。
title_zh: 认证机构在奥利弗大学迁至密苏里州后批准了该校的20个项目
author: Christian Daily International

title: Top 3 things to know about James Talarico's girlfriend: 'She is my rock'

summary_zh: 以下是关于当选参议员James Talarico的女友Brianna Menard的一些最值得了解的信息，她因从低调的生活中崭露头角而备受关注。
title_zh: 关于James Talarico女友的3大要点：“她是我的坚强后盾”
author: CP Staff

title: 56% of parents want AI fully blocked in schools. Will anyone listen?
summary: Parents have heard the promises before. They watched schools pour $30 billion into Chromebooks and tablets as achievement fell. Now they're being asked to trust AI, and most aren't ready to.
summary_zh: 家长们以前也听过这样的承诺。他们眼睁睁地看着学校在学业成绩下滑之际，将300亿美元投入到Chromebook和平板电脑上。现在，他们被要求信任人工智能，但大多数人还没有做好准备。
title_zh: 56%的家长希望在学校完全禁止使用人工智能。有人会听取他们的意见吗？
author: Melissa Henson

title: From George Washington to a postponed parade: 7 Thanksgiving records and milestones
summary: President George Washington set the first national Thanksgiving for Nov. 26, the same date as this year's observance. Here are seven records and milestones from the holiday's history, including a first for the Macy's parade.
summary_zh: 乔治·华盛顿总统将第一个全国感恩节定在11月26日，与今年的庆祝日期相同。以下是这个节日历史上的七项纪录和里程碑，其中包括梅西百货游行的首次亮相。
title_zh: 从乔治·华盛顿到推迟的游行：7项感恩节纪录和里程碑
author: Michael Gryboski

title: This Thanksgiving, Americans are more grateful — but to whom?
summary: Americans say they are more grateful than ever. Neither of this year's major gratitude surveys mentions God, and that silence may be the most revealing finding of all.
summary_zh: 美国人表示，他们比以往任何时候都更加感恩。今年两项主要的感恩调查均未提及上帝，而这种沉默或许是最能说明问题的一个发现。
title_zh: 今年的感恩节，美国人更加感恩——但他们感恩的对象是谁？
author: Virgil Walker

title: The Word Made Flesh: New 75-Song Advent Playlist
summary: Brett McCracken curates a low-key collection of songs meant to draw you into doctrinal reflection this Advent.
summary_zh: 基督快乐! 就像我大多数年头一样,我整理了一张新的手选歌曲播放列表,以帮助丰富你在这个神圣季节的经历. 今年的播放列表以约翰1:1–14为灵感的“The Word Made Flesh”为主题。 在Spotify或Apple Music上找到75首歌曲的播放列表.
title_zh: 道成肉身：75首新歌组成的将临期播放列表
content: Happy Advent! As I do most years, I curated a new playlist of hand-picked songs to help enrich your experience of this sacred season. This year’s playlist is themed “The Word Made Flesh,” inspired by John 1:1–14. Find the 75-song playlist on Spotify or Apple Music . I picked songs that celebrate the mind-blowing theological reality of incarnation, the Word who “became flesh and dwelt among us” (v. 14). The first part of the Gospel of John has always been among my favorite sections of Scripture, and several songs on this playlist pull directly from these profound biblical words. John’s emphasis on the imagery of light also figures prominently in my song selection. Tonally, this is a more low-key, subdued collection of songs, featuring contemplative and instrumental songs meant to draw you into doctrinal reflection. I included a number of sacred choral works alongside new renditions of old carols and hymns like “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing,” “Come Thou Long Expected Jesus,” and the ancient Prudentius poem, “Of the Father’s Love Begotten.” I tried to set a “cozy fireplace on cold December nights” mood, with plenty of jazz, folk, and low-fi sounds (and not much in the way of Christian pop radio). This can be a stressful and harried season, so I picked songs that cultivate calm. I pray the worshipful vibe of this playlist fosters quiet devotional reflection for you and your family as you journey through Advent toward Christmas. title: Christmas Is Good News for the Headline Weary
summary: There’s no better news than the gospel—the message that God sent his Son to die on a cross for our sins and open a way for us to be reconciled to him.

title_zh: 圣诞节对于厌倦头条新闻的人来说是个好消息
content: Read Go on up to a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good news; lift up your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, herald of good news; lift it up, fear not; say to the cities of Judah, “Behold your God!” (Isa. 40:9) Reflect When I first started writing for The Gospel Coalition, my editor told me we were going to report good news. We were going to tell stories of where Christians were helping and the kingdom was advancing. We were going to say, “Behold, church, how God is at work in the world!” Neither of us had a lot of confidence it’d work. We have education and experience in journalism, and we know there’s a reason joy, peace, and cooperation aren’t often featured in articles. Nobody reads those stories. There’s a reason joy, peace, and cooperation aren’t often featured in articles. Nobody reads those stories. That’s not because humans are insensitive monsters. It’s because when we read bad news, our bodies react with fight or flight instincts— studies show our hearts beat faster and our skin begins to perspire. We want to understand or process what’s going on, so we click on the link and read past the headline. When we read good news, on the other hand, we have no physiological response. Heart rates and perspiration levels stay the same. Researchers say it’s the same nonresponse we have when we look at a blank screen. For a long time, I was frustrated with God for creating us this way. Why didn’t he make us able to absorb bad news calmly and react to good news with wild, enthusiastic joy? Wouldn’t that be better? Wouldn’t that make Isaiah’s job easier? And John the Baptist’s? And Jesus’s? Wouldn’t that make the church’s job easier? “Behold your God!” we could say to the world. “Isn’t he amazing? Isn’t it wonderful what he has done for us?” And the secular world would shout back, “Hooray! Praise the Lord!” But that’s not how God did it. And only recently did I begin to spot the beauty in his way. First, it’s right that human bodies react with stress and anxiety to news of sin and brokenness in the world. That’s a sign we were made for another world, one that isn’t steeped in corruption and sadness. It’s a testimony that God himself, the One we image, doesn’t ignore evil. The tension we feel is a tiny shadow of God’s reaction when he sees depravity unfolding across space and time. Second, just because we stay relaxed when reading good reports or stories doesn’t mean we’re unaffected. Studies show that when we hear positive news, we’re not only happier but more likely to take action —to respond with compassion and energy to the world around us. There’s no better news than the gospel—the message that God sent his Son to die on a cross for our sins and open a way for us to be reconciled to him. Our good God offers us not only salvation from our past but purpose for our present and hope for our future. Our good God offers us not only salvation from our past but purpose for our present and hope for our future. This good news changed, and continues to change, the world. Out of grateful joy, Christians have become missionaries, started schools, and adopted children. They’ve moved to broken places, given away their time and money, and forgiven those who sinned against them. They’ve preached the gospel, made countercultural choices, and kept doggedly working long before they saw any fruit. Behold, our God! What marvelous things he has done in us, is doing through us, and has planned for us. Respond Consider your news diet. If good news energizes us, how can you limit your bad news intake or find more good news? How can you keep reminding yourself of the good news of the gospel?

title: ‘Confession’ and ‘Ebenezer’: Moral Clarity in Murky Times
summary: New movies ‘Confession’ and ‘Ebenezer’ unmask the ugliness of secular ‘values.’ They celebrate Christian virtue and the way grace transforms a life.
summary_zh: 当代 好莱坞未必以道德清晰著称。 今天的电影往往看起来不错,但却缺乏一致的信念; 电影在艺术上可能优秀,但在道德上破产。 或相反者能真实.
title_zh: “忏悔”与“埃比尼泽”：混沌时代的道德明晰
content: Contemporary Hollywood isn’t necessarily known for moral clarity. More often than not, today’s movies look good but lack coherent convictions; they might be artistically excellent but morally bankrupt . Or the opposite can be true. The movies that do have moral clarity are often aesthetically bland: didactic, unsubtle, cheesy. Every so often, though, movies appear that are compelling to watch, artistically strong, entertaining, and morally commendable. Two new releases like this are Confession and Ebenezer . I went into these movies with low expectations, but both surprised me in good ways. They’re very different films tonally and topically. And while certainly not perfect, they share a refreshingly clear moral vision. Both unmask the ugliness and emptiness of secular “values.” Both celebrate Christian virtue and the way grace transforms a life. As we celebrate Thanksgiving in the United States this week, I’m thankful movies like this are still being made. I commend them to you and your family if you’re looking for edifying stories to watch over the holidays. Confession Shows Christian Courage Under Pressure Confession has a cast full of veteran actors (Rob Lowe, James Franco, Emile Hirsch, Nick Nolte, Jennifer Jason Leigh) but couldn’t find a distributor in Hollywood because the movie’s script is written by Ben Shapiro, a well-known political conservative. In the progressive hegemony of Hollywood, you’ll get canceled or blacklisted for associating with or saying nice things about conservative-made movies. Thus, Confession can only be seen on The Daily Wire , and only six film critics (as of this writing) even bothered to publish reviews of it on Rotten Tomatoes . As some reactions to Fjord revealed earlier this year, viewpoint diversity in Hollywood is limited. “Representation matters!” is the mantra, but arguably the most underrepresented viewpoints in Hollywood—religious and political conservatives—continue to be marginalized. Hollywood feels threatened by conservatives bringing their perspectives to art. Why else would it blacklist movies like Confession ? The irony is that Confession is a movie about leftist regimes suppressing dissenting views as a way to maintain narrative control. So perhaps it’s appropriate that the industry’s reaction is proving the movie’s point. Directed by Czech filmmaker Václav Marhoul, Confession is a strange little movie. It feels at times like a filmed stage play. The chamber drama takes place in confined, claustrophobic, dimly lit spaces and is entirely driven by long, lofty conversations about philosophy, literature, art, and politics. It’s like a Richard Linklater film with Russians who speak with American accents. The film’s pacing is slow. And while the performances are good, it’s not an easy movie to watch. Some viewers won’t be able to sit through Confession’ s 130-minute duration, but it’s rewarding if you do. The film’s central protagonist, Alexei (Rob Lowe), is a former literature professor who converted to Christianity and now—in Stalin’s 1938 Moscow—speaks the dangerous truth that “Christ is above the party.” It’s a truth—as prophetic today as it was then—that lands him in the Lubyanka Prison, where he’s interrogated by former student Vladimir (James Franco). Will Alexei relent and save himself, or will he keep his integrity and pay a significant price? At times, Confession reminded me of Sophie Scholl (2005) or A Hidden Life (2019), movies that capture the high cost Christian dissenters pay when they stand up to oppressive secular regimes. Having found Christ, Alexei sacrifices his livelihood and even his familial attachments for the sake of his Savior. Why? Because he believes in truth and beauty beyond this world. Alexei sacrifices his livelihood and even his familial attachments for the sake of his Savior. Why? Because he believes in truth and beauty beyond this world. While his interrogator and some fellow prisoners mock him for his “opiate of the masses” beliefs, Alexei insists that we’re more than just rotting flesh and that there’s a moral logic beyond brute power. Though at times Shapiro’s script feels excessively talky and at times maybe preachy, the discursive dialogue is regularly profound. Heavily influenced by (and frequently quoting) Dostoevsky, the film’s script engages big questions about theodicy, power, beauty, and faith. The film starkly juxtaposes an atheistic socialist regime, where government is the “savior” and promises material provision and security, and Christianity, where the person of Christ saves us and promises eternal life. The latter provides a basis for art, beauty, literature, and joy. The former leads only to a reductionist materialism where work, bread, and the state are the sum of existential meaning. “What do you believe in?” Alexei asks a Stalinist in the film. “Bread,” he replies. Alexei argues that selfhood goes beyond survival. “To be a man, you have to believe in something greater than the party, greater than steel and power and machines and iron foundries, greater even than bread. You must believe in what it means to be a man.” Confession isn’t perfect, but it displays the power of a man who believes in “something greater than the party.” In this way, the movie isn’t the partisan polemic progressives assume it is. Shapiro is critiquing anyone —left or right—who sees “the party” as his or her primary source of hope and meaning. The secular transcendence of political power is insidious on all sides, in all eras. Confession calls us to a higher truth—one that gives our lives real meaning, purpose, and hope. Ebenezer Shows the Transforming Power of Grace The trailer and marketing for Ebenezer make it look like a goofy, childish, irreverent version of the classic Charles Dickens novella, A Christmas Carol . But the movie is one of the most faithful adaptations yet, as morally serious and clear as any cinematic take on the story. Yes, Johnny Depp is very “Johnny Depp” in the titular role. His portrayal of the infamous miser is full-bodied, quirky, and fun. He infuses both humor and heart into an iconic role that has been played by George C. Scott, Albert Finney, James Earl Jones, Michael Caine, Patrick Stewart, Kelsey Grammer, Jim Carrey, and Guy Pearce, to name but a few. This latest adaptation is directed by Ti West, most known for his direction of horror movies. West’s macabre sensibility fits the Dickens story well, which is full of Victorian gothic elements and the “hauntings” of various ghosts. For some younger viewers, the apparitions in this movie—Jacob Marley, and the ghosts of Christmas past, present, and future—will be a bit too scary. But for older kids and adults, this classic tale isn’t just a spooky story vividly told; it has much virtue to teach. Similarly to Confession , Ebenezer clearly juxtaposes two dispositions: a scarcity-mindset materialism, where life and love are subordinated to a joyless quest for mere survival, and a grace-based abundance, where hardship is reframed by gospel hope and generosity flows freely out of gratitude for what we have—but don’t deserve. A Christmas Carol is one of the great stories of character transformation. To watch Scrooge’s redemption journey—which climaxes in a literal scene of rebirth out of the grave (“I’m not the man I was!”)—is to see Christian theology enacted. New birth: the old self put off, the new self put on. The effect of the Christmas Eve warnings on Scrooge is profound. It’s not just that his cold greed melts away into warm generosity. It’s that his calculated, merciless accounting of life (“Life has always been a cruel and miserable affair”)—based on an unforgiving ledger that would relegate even the kindhearted Bob Cratchit (Rupert Grint) to debtors’ prison—gives way to a view of life framed by abundance and grace. He comes to see that true freedom isn’t independence but interdependence, not earning and hoarding but loving and being loved. To watch Scrooge’s redemption journey—which climaxes in

当代 好莱坞未必以道德清晰著称。 今天的电影往往看起来不错,但却缺乏一致的信念;电影在艺术上可能优秀,但在道德上破产。 或相反者能真实. 具有道德清晰度的电影往往在美学上是粗俗的:戏剧性的,不显眼的,俗气的.
不过,电影经常出现,这些电影令人望而却步,艺术性强,娱乐性强,在道德上值得赞扬。 这样的两个新版本是忏悔和Ebenezer。 我进入这些电影 低期望,但两者 令我惊讶的方式。 他们的影片与众不同, 尽管他们肯定不完美,但他们有着清晰的道德观。
揭开世俗“价值”的丑恶和空虚。 既要颂扬基督教的美德,也要颂扬恩典改变生活的方式. 这星期我们在美国庆祝感恩节, 我向你和你的家人推荐,
忏悔显示基督教勇气在压力下的忏悔, 里面装满了老牌演员(Rob Lowe、James Franco、Emile Hirsch、Nick Nolte、Jennifer Jason Leigh),
在好莱坞的进步霸权中,你会因为与保守制电影有关或说好话而被取消或列入黑名单。 也只有六位影评人(至此为止)在罗腾番茄上发表评论。
正如今年早些时候对Fjord的一些反应所揭示的那样,好莱坞的观点多样性是有限的。 “代表重要!”是口号,但可以说是好莱坞最代表不足的观点——宗教和政治保守派——继续被边缘化。 好莱坞感觉受到保守派将视角带到艺术上的威胁.
否则为什么它会黑名单 电影如忏悔? 讽刺的是,忏悔是一部关于左翼政权压制不同意见的电影,作为保持叙事控制的一种方式. 或许产业界的反应能证明电影的观点, 由捷克电影制片人瓦茨拉夫·马胡尔执导,忏悔是一部奇特的小电影. 有时感觉像被拍摄的舞台剧.
室内剧情发生在封闭的,幽闭的,淡淡的空间中,完全由关于哲学,文学,艺术和政治的长篇崇高对话所驱动. 这就像理查德·林克利特的电影, 影片的节奏缓慢. 虽然表演不错,
有些观众无法通过忏悔时间130分钟,
这部电影的中心主角阿列克谢(英语:Alexei (Rob Lowe))是一位前文学教授,他皈依基督教,现在的斯大林1938年的莫斯科,他讲出了危险的真理:"基督高于党". 他被前学生弗拉基米尔(James Franco)审问。
阿列克谢会放纵并自救,还是保持正直,付出重大代价? 有时,忏悔让我想起Sophie Schol(2005年)或A Hidden Life(2019年),这些电影记录了基督教异议者在反抗压迫性世俗政权时付出的高昂代价。
在找到基督后,阿列克谢为了救世主牺牲了自己的生计,甚至牺牲了家人的依恋. 为什么? 因为他相信这个世界以外的真理和美 阿列克谢为了救世主牺牲了自己的生计,甚至牺牲了家人的依恋. 为什么? 因为他相信这个世界以外的真理和美
阿列克谢坚持认为我们不仅仅是腐烂的肉体, 还有一个超越野蛮力量的道德逻辑。 虽然有时Shapiro的剧本过于空谈, 有时甚至可能讲道,
受(并经常引用)严重影响 Dostoevsky,这部电影的剧本涉及关于神学,权力,美和信仰的大问题. 这部电影严酷地将无神论社会主义政权和基督教并列,政府是“救主”,承诺物质供给和安全,基督教是基督拯救我们和保证永生的。
后者为艺术,美貌,文学,欢乐提供了基础. 前者只导致一种简化主义唯物主义,其中工作,面包,国家是存在意义的总和. “你相信什么?” 阿列克谢在电影中问斯大林主义者. 他回答说,“面包”。 阿列克谢认为,自我主义超越了生存.
“要成为一个男人,就必须相信比党更伟大、比钢铁、电力、机器和铁铸造厂更伟大、甚至比面包更伟大的东西。 你必须相信做人的意义。” 忏悔并非完美无缺,但它显示了一个相信“比党更大的东西”的人的力量。 这部电影不是党派争斗进步者认为的。
沙皮罗将任何视“党”为希望和意义之主要源泉的人——无论是左派还是右派的人——都吓坏了。 政治权力的世俗超越在所有方面,在所有时代都是阴险的。 忏悔要求我们寻求一个更高的真理——一个赋予我们生命真正意义、目的和希望的真理。
Ebenezer 展现了恩典的变幻力量 Ebenezer的预告片和营销使得它看起来像一个愚蠢的,幼稚的,不道德的版本经典的查尔斯·狄更斯小说"圣诞卡罗尔". 但这部电影是最忠实的改编作品之一, 道德上严肃而清晰, 任何电影家都接受这个故事。 是的,约翰尼·德普非常“强尼·德普”在三角角色。
他描绘的臭名昭著的沉闷 充满了活力和乐趣 他把幽默和心灵都注入到一个标志性角色中,由乔治·C·斯科特,阿尔伯特·芬尼,詹姆斯·厄尔·琼斯,迈克尔·凯恩,帕特里克·斯图尔特,凯尔西·格拉姆默,吉姆·卡里,以及盖伊·皮尔斯(英语:Guy Pearce)担任,仅举几个例子. 这一最新改编由Ti West执导,最以恐怖电影的方向著称.
West的macabre 感性很符合狄更斯的故事, 充满维多利亚式的哥特式元素, 对于一些年轻观众来说,这部电影中的寓意——Jacob Marley,以及圣诞过去,现在和未来的鬼魂——会有点太可怕了. 但对于年长的孩子和成年人来说,
它有很多优点可以教 Ebenezer显然将两种倾向相提并论:一种是匮乏的唯物主义, 生活和爱服从于对仅仅生存的无趣追求,
圣诞卡罗尔是角色转变的伟大故事之一. 看着史克罗格的救赎之旅——这段旅程在坟墓复活的一瞬间达到了高潮(“我不是我曾经的人!”)——就是看到基督教神学的制定。 新出生:旧的自我推迟,新的自我穿上. 平安夜警告对史克罗格的影响是深远的.
他的冷酷贪婪不仅融化为热情的慷慨。 他对生活(生活总是残酷和悲惨的)的精心计算、无情的记述——基于一个不可饶恕的分类账,即使善良的Bob Cratchit(Rupert Grint)也会被降格为债务人的监狱,
他发现真正的自由不是独立而是相互依存, 看着史克罗格的救赎之旅,
author: Brett McCracken

title: Why I’m Thankful for Evangelical Publishing
summary: The spread of the gospel and the church’s survival isn’t dependent on the state of publishing. But having quality books on spiritual formation, theology, and church practice makes equipping the saints easier.
summary_zh: 在我担任福音联盟的书籍编辑工作一年左右, 我和我的邮差交叉了道路, 他把另一盒书拖到我的门廊。 他问:“你读了很多吗? ” 我笑了起来。 我收到一连串的书籍, 主要是福音报社的书籍, 出版商希望我考虑审查或推广。
title_zh: 我为何感谢福音派出版物
content: Around a year into my job as books editor for The Gospel Coalition, I crossed paths with my mailman as he lugged yet another box of books to my front porch. “Do you read much?” he asked. I laughed. I receive a steady stream of books, mainly from evangelical presses, that publishers want me to consider for review or promotion. In many cases, when people ask me for a book recommendation on a specific topic, I have a handful of theologically sound and readable options to choose from. But that’s not the case for many Christians around the world. This summer, I travelled to Brazil to teach a graduate course in Christian ethics. Unfortunately, none of my preferred textbooks—the ones that most closely match my approach to ethics—were available in Portuguese. In English, I have half a dozen good options to choose from. I ended up requiring a translation of John Murray’s Principles of Conduct , which is solid but dated. Though more than 47 million Brazilians identify as evangelical and Portuguese is one of the most commonly spoken languages in the world, there are significant gaps among the available Christian resources. The abundance of books that many American evangelicals enjoy is a result of our Protestant heritage, but we shouldn’t take it for granted. Protestant Publishing Christianity is a religion of the book. Not only were early Christians devoted to the texts of the Old and New Testaments, but they also wrote many apologetic and doctrinal texts. Those early Christians were among the first adopters of the codex (what we think of as the book)—one of the rare times that the church has been a leader in technological innovation. Despite claims to the contrary, Christians were also instrumental in preserving pagan literature. As Thomas Cahill argues , “Without the Mission of the Irish Monks . . . the world that came after them would have been an entirely different one—a world without books.” And, of course, the Protestant Reformation was catalyzed by Gutenberg’s invention of movable type, which turned books and pamphlets into mass media. Had Luther’s Ninety-five Theses not been distributed to the masses by German printers, the emphasis on justification by faith alone and Scripture’s final authority might have been much slower to take root. This year, we’re celebrating the 500th anniversary of William Tyndale’s New Testament translation, an accomplishment that helped create the English language as we know it. Famously, Tyndale’s goal was to help the plowboy in the field know more of God than the religious elites did. That required ready access to Scripture and the ability to read, both of which became emphases among descendants of the Reformation. Protestant missionaries helped make rising literacy a worldwide phenomenon. As political scientist Robert Woodberry argues , “[Conversionary Protestants] advocated mass literacy so that everyone could read the Bible and interpret it competently. Their attempt to convert people through education threatened other elites and spurred these elites to also invest in mass education.” Literacy for the purpose of discipleship was a rising tide that lifted all boats. Protestant missionaries helped make rising literacy a worldwide phenomenon. It’s little wonder that American neo-evangelicals like Billy Graham and Carl F. H. Henry made publishing a priority in the 20th century by founding magazines and book publishers. To some degree, the health of a religious movement depends on the availability of religious resources in print. Worldwide Evangelical Publishing Although I was disappointed by the available options for a core ethics textbook in Portuguese, there are reasons to be encouraged about global publishing. While I was teaching in Brazil, I met with a local Baptist pastor who started a new publishing house, Pro Nobis Editora , in 2018 and has since published more than 120 books. Many have been translated from English, but some were written in Portuguese. Another Brazilian publisher, Editora Fiel , has been faithfully publishing Reformed and evangelical books since 1966, with a much longer list of titles. Though they represent two different traditions, the two ministries cooperate to address key issues facing pastors in the continent-sized country that is Brazil. They hold conferences to equip and encourage pastors with books that address key spiritual needs of the diverse nation. We have a lot to be thankful for. Nevertheless, according to Tiago Santos, CEO of Editora Fiel, “Many important areas of biblical and theological literature remain insufficiently covered, and the demand for sound resources continues to grow, not only in Brazil but also in Portuguese-speaking countries in Africa, where access to theological books is often particularly limited.” The same mix of challenge and encouragement exists for faithful evangelical publishers around the world. Last year, Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra wrote about a growing Reformed book publisher in Alexandria, Egypt. She also highlighted gospel-centered publishers working to outprint the prosperity gospel in Southern Africa. And she interviewed missionary and church planter Aleksander Saško Nezamutdinov, whose church is fighting to resource Ukrainian Christians with books. Read Gratefully There’s plenty of encouraging news about Christian publishing around the world. We should celebrate the important work international publishers are doing to serve the church with original and translated gospel-centered resources. We should also thank God for the abundance of theologically sound resources we have in the English-speaking world. When I walk through the exhibition hall at the Evangelical Theological Society, I’m encouraged by the depth and breadth of scholarship by Christians who affirm Scripture’s inerrancy. That wasn’t always the case. It’s taken decades for some of our most trusted publishers to grow into what we recognize today . But the success of evangelical publishing brings a danger. It’s easy to take the health of our publishers for granted. The number of American adults who read at least one complete book in a year has declined over the past decades. Short-form video is grabbing more of our attention and taking up time that could be used for other activities, including reading books. Our media consumption is making it harder and harder to focus on the sorts of arguments the best Christian books make: well-reasoned and carefully researched. We should celebrate the important work international publishers are doing to serve the church with original and translated gospel-centered resources. English-speaking Christians need to work to preserve the publishers that serve us well. Even confessional and mission-driven publishers have to respond to market signals. If evangelical Christians don’t buy and read the good books being published, the list of future titles will shrink. If we don’t recommend the books we love and critique the ones we don’t, they’ll publish whatever they like or whatever sells. It usually takes much longer to build an institution than to lose one. The spread of the gospel and the church’s survival isn’t dependent on the state of publishing. But having quality books on spiritual formation, theology, and church practice makes equipping the saints easier. We should pray for and look for ways to partner with evangelical publishers around the world. Even if it leads to awkward conversations with the mailman, we should also be thankful for the abundance of resources available in our own language.
content_zh:
在我担任福音联盟的书籍编辑工作一年左右, 我和我的邮差交叉了道路, 他把另一盒书拖到我的门廊。 他问:“你读了很多吗?” 我笑了起来。 我收到一连串的书籍, 主要是福音报社的书籍, 出版商希望我考虑审查或推广。
在许多情况下,当人们问我关于特定主题的书推荐时,我有一些神学上健全和可读的选择,可以从中选择. 但世界各地许多基督徒的情况并非如此。 今年夏天,我前往巴西讲授基督教伦理学的研究生课程。
不幸的是,我最喜欢的教科书——最符合我对道德的态度的教科书——都没有葡萄牙文版本。 在英语中,我有六打好的选择 我最后需要约翰·默里(John Murray)的《行为原则》翻译,
尽管4 700多万巴西人确认福音派和葡萄牙语是世界上最常用的语言之一,但现有基督教资源差距很大。 许多美国福音派教徒所喜爱的书籍丰富, 是我们新教传统的结果,
新教出版基督教是该书的一个宗教. 早期基督徒不仅致力于"旧约"和"新约"的文本,还撰写了许多古典和学说文本. 这些早期的基督徒是法典(我们认为是这本书)最早的采纳者之一,这是教会在技术革新方面最罕见的一次。
尽管有相反的说法,基督徒在保存异教文学方面也起了作用. 正如托马斯·卡希尔指出,“没有爱尔兰僧侣的使命......。
在他们之后的世界,将是一个完全不同的世界,一个没有书的世界。 当然,新教改革是由古腾堡发明的可移动类型催化的,它把书籍和小册子变成了大众媒体.
如果路德的95本论文没有被德国的印刷商散发给大众,那么仅仅通过信仰和圣经的最终权威来强调理由就可能更慢一些。 今年,我们正在庆祝威廉·廷达勒新约翻译500周年,这一成就帮助创造了我们所知道的英语。
与宗教精英相比, Tyndale 的目标是帮助田间耕田男孩更多地了解上帝。 这需要随时获得《圣经》和阅读能力,两者都成为改革后后代的重点。 新教传教士帮助使提高识字率成为全球现象。
正如政治学家罗伯特·伍德伯里(Robert Woodberry)所认为的那样,“皈依新教徒”提倡大众识字,以便人人都能阅读圣经,并能够胜任地解释圣经。 他们试图通过教育使人民皈依,这威胁到其他精英阶层,促使这些精英阶层也投资于大众教育。” 为弟子化目的识字是一个上升的潮流,它抬起所有船只。
新教传教士帮助使提高识字率成为全球现象。 美国新福音派人士如比利·格雷厄姆(Billy Graham)和卡尔·H·亨利(Carl F. H. Henry), 将出版列为20世纪创刊杂志和书籍出版商的优先工作, 在某种程度上,宗教运动的健康取决于是否有印刷的宗教资源。
虽然我对葡萄牙语核心道德教科书的现有选择感到失望, 我在巴西执教期间,会见了当地浸信会牧师,他在2018年创办了一家新的出版社Pro Nobis Editora,此后出版了120多本书。
许多是用英语翻译的,但有些是用葡萄牙语写的。 另一家巴西出版商Editora Fiel自1966年以来一直忠实地出版经过改革的福音书,其标题清单更长。 虽然这两个部代表着两种不同的传统,但这两个部合作处理巴西这个大陆大小国家的牧师所面临的关键问题。
他们举行会议,为牧师配备和鼓励他们编写书籍,满足不同民族的主要精神需要。 我们有很多事情需要感谢。
然而,Editora Fiel的首席执行官蒂亚戈·桑托斯(Tiago Santos)认为,“圣经和神学文献的许多重要领域仍没有得到充分的涵盖,对健全资源的需求继续增长,不仅在巴西,而且在非洲葡萄牙语国家,获得神学书籍的机会往往特别有限。” 挑战与鼓励的组合也相同。
全世界忠实的福音派出版社。 去年Sarah Eekhoff Zylstra在埃及亚历山大写道, 她还着重指出,以福音为中心的出版商努力印刷南部非洲繁荣的福音。
她采访了传教士和教会规划师Aleksander Saško Nezamutdinov, 他的教堂正在努力为乌克兰基督徒提供书籍。 愉快地阅读 世界各地有许多关于基督教出版的令人鼓舞的消息。 我们应该庆祝国际出版商为教会服务所做的重要工作,提供以福音为中心的原始和翻译资源。
我们还应当感谢上帝为我们在英语世界拥有大量神学上健全的资源。 我对基督教徒奖学金的深度和广度感到鼓舞, 情况并非总是如此。
我们的一些最信任的出版商花了几十年才成长为我们今天所认识的。 但福音派出版的成功带来了危险. 我们的出版商的健康是理所当然的。 在过去几十年中,一年中至少读过一本完整书的美国成年人数量有所下降.
短视频吸引了我们更多的注意力,占用了可用于其他活动,包括阅读书籍的时间。 我们的媒体消费使得人们越来越难以关注基督教书籍中最优秀的论调:合理和认真的研究。
我们应该庆祝国际出版商为教会服务所做的重要工作,提供以福音为中心的原始和翻译资源。 说英语的基督徒需要努力保护那些为我们服务得很好的出版商. 甚至连忏悔和使命驱动的出版商都要响应市场信号.
如果福音派基督徒不购买和阅读即将出版的优秀书籍,未来标题的列表将会萎缩. 如果我们不推荐我们喜爱的书籍, 建立机构通常比失去机构需要更长的时间。
福音的传播和教会的生存并不取决于出版状况。 但拥有关于精神形成,神学,和教会实践的优质书籍,使得圣人更容易获得装备. 我们应该祈祷和寻找与世界各地福音出版商合作的方法。
即使这会导致与邮递员的尴尬交谈,我们也应当感谢以我们自己的语言提供的大量资源。
author: Andrew Spencer

title: The Church Needs to Know Its History
summary: Readers of this first volume of ‘Church History for Everyone’ won’t get a complete understanding of church history, but DeYoung provides a doorway through which ordinary Christians can learn to explore primary sources and more comprehensive surveys on their own.
summary_zh: 我的Facebook留言的档案里 藏着一个叫凯西的寡妇的遗言 她感谢我在我们的每周圣经研究中使用了教会历史. 她喜欢了解早期教会的烈士和朝圣者. 作为一位在教会历史中攻读博士学位的资深牧师,这是我需要的保证。 我们的信息线结束 凯西描述她的化疗。
title_zh: 教会需要了解自己的历史
content: Deep in the archives of my Facebook messages sits a note from a widow named Kathy. She thanked me for using church history in our weekly Bible studies. She loved learning about the early-church martyrs and the pilgrims. As a newly minted senior pastor pursuing a PhD in church history, this was the reassurance I needed. Our message thread ended with Kathy describing her chemo treatments. Like Faithful in John Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (a story new to her that strengthened her fight with cancer), Kathy endured her trials and entered the Celestial City. I usually have to defend the benefits of history to other pastors and friends of mine—but rarely with church members. I mostly encounter excitement when I direct Christians to our family history. In Church History for Everyone: The Story of Christianity from the Fall of Jerusalem to the Dawn of the Reformation , Kevin DeYoung, pastor of Christ Covenant Church and associate professor of systematic theology at Reformed Theological Seminary (Charlotte), blends rich doctrine with a pastoral tone. It’s the first of two planned volumes. DeYoung writes, “I intend this book to be a popular history rather than professional history, which means I am writing to be understood by ordinary people who are eager to learn but are not experts” (3). He’s successful in that effort. I wish Kathy could have read this book; it’s a church history for the church. History for the Church How is church history for the church actually for the church ? Well, words on a page are costly. Just like a pastor needs to cut more of his preparation and study out of his sermons than he’d like, a church history book for everyday Christians needs to value the reader’s attention. This means accepting that not every believer has the bandwidth to process all the names and details from church history we might want him or her to. There’s so much to digest, and the practical value of these names, dates, and specialized terms often don’t stick in the minds of casual readers. It’s easy for the stay-at-home mom or busy mechanic to delve into a church history book and quickly lose steam. On the other hand, oversimplifying in an attempt to make a book more accessible can move an argument from truth and falsehood. The story of our past needs the proper names, dates, and details to lead readers to experience the fruit of good historical learning. DeYoung attempts a near-impossible task: to write an introduction to church history that’s true (factually sound), good (encourages the church), and beautiful (enjoyable to read). He checks those boxes. Biographical Emphasis The most compelling histories are told through people, not periods. That explains why, “instead of a chronological encyclopedia version of history,” DeYoung takes “a biographical approach” (6). We get stories about figures like Irenaeus, Perpetua and Felicity, Athanasius, and Jan Hus. We read of Hus, As a pastor, Hus was passionate and sometimes hotheaded. His sermons also displayed a witty sense of humor. . . . Compared to most men of his age, he was not poor, but neither did he amass any fortune or have family estates to retire to. Even later when his enemies charged him with many faults and crimes, they never charged him with the typical list of priestly sins: drunkenness, sexual immorality, laziness, or opulence. (351) This approach has downsides, of course. A lot of important information gets left out. However, DeYoung recognizes that “when the author tells a story, there is a better chance that the reader might keep reading” (8). The most compelling histories are told through people. The biographical approach reinforces the fact that history often isn’t just about information transfer. “The goal in telling church history has been—for most of church history—a deliberate attempt at inspiration,” DeYoung observes. For example, “[Athanasius] wanted Christians in the fourth century to reach the inescapable conclusion that Antony was a hero, and that what he believed and how he lived had immediate lessons for followers of Christ everywhere” (71–72). From the earliest centuries, Christians have told the stories of other Christians. Accounts of Polycarp’s martyrdom to Foxe’s Book of Martyrs have inspired faithfulness for centuries. In recent years, John Piper’s short biographies and Stephen Nichols’s 5 Minutes in Church History podcast have awakened new appreciation for deeper studies of the past among laypeople. When we study church history, our doctrines and interpretations don’t remain in the abstract but get attached to names, faces, and places. We learn to see how our lives participate in the grand story of God thwarting Satan’s attempts to overwhelm the church. Novel Contribution Though a number of solid introductions to church history already exist, this first volume of Church History for Everyone fills an important niche. Almost every seminarian who has taken a class on the history of Christianity is familiar with Justo L. González’s two-volume The Story of Christianity . These works have offered classrooms a standard introduction to church history for more than 40 years. However, I’ve never directed church members to these works because they clock in around 1,000 pages total and include a lot of details about people, places, and events, without much theological commentary. We learn to see how our lives participate in the grand story of God thwarting Satan’s attempts to overwhelm the church. Many of God’s people want more than facts and narrative. This is why I’ve recommended Bruce Shelley’s Church History in Plain Language or Nick Needham’s five-volume 2,000 Years of Christ’s Power . Shelley writes with great clarity. Needham masterfully weaves the flow of church history with insight and precision. But I still offer caveats when recommending these works to church members because, as plain as the writing may be, the content is dense and filled with the nuance, historical data, and name indexes that stretch multiple pages. A chasm yawns between the academy and the pews that leaves many Christians wondering whether they’re looking at a textbook when they see it’s got “church history” on the cover. DeYoung demonstrates remarkable discipline as a trained historian as he writes this book by leaving many footnotes, narrative rabbit trails, and theological debates out of the final product. But that’s what makes this book so useful. Readers of this first volume of Church History for Everyone won’t get a complete understanding of church history, but DeYoung provides a doorway through which ordinary Christians can learn to explore primary sources and more comprehensive surveys on their own. I only wish that Kathy could have read this book; it would have helped sustain her on the journey to the Celestial City.
content_zh:
我的Facebook留言的档案里 藏着一个叫凯西的寡妇的遗言 她感谢我在我们的每周圣经研究中使用了教会历史. 她喜欢了解早期教会的烈士和朝圣者. 作为一位在教会历史中攻读博士学位的资深牧师,这是我需要的保证。 我们的信息线结束 凯西描述她的化疗。
就像忠实于约翰·邦扬的朝圣者进步(她的新故事加强了她与癌症的战斗)一样,凯西忍受了她的考验并进入了天城。 我通常不得不为其他牧师和朋友捍卫历史利益, 当我把基督徒引向家族历史时,我大多会遇到兴奋。
在《人人教会历史:从耶路撒冷沦陷到改革黎明的基督教故事》中,Kevin DeYoung,基督盟约教会牧师和改革神学院(夏洛特)系统神学副教授,将丰富的学说与牧歌融合在一起。 这是两卷计划书中的第一卷。
DeYoung写道:“我打算这本书是一部受欢迎的历史,而不是专业历史,这意味着我写作是为了让渴望学习但并非专家的普通人理解。” (3)。 他的努力是成功的。 我希望凯西能读到这本书, 教会的历史是怎样的 教会的历史实际上是教会?
嗯,一页上的话是昂贵的。 就像牧师在布道中需要减少他的准备和学习, 这意味着接受并非每个信徒都有带宽来处理我们可能希望他或她处理的教会历史中所有的名字和细节.
这些名称、日期和专门术语的实际价值往往不会停留在临时读者的脑海里。 家庭妈妈或繁忙的技工, 另一方面,为了使一本书更容易获得而过分简化,可以使一个论点从真理和谎言中转移出来。
我们过去的故事需要适当的名字,日期,细节,以引导读者体验良好的历史学习成果. DeYoung试图完成一个近乎不可能的任务:写一个教会历史的介绍,这个介绍是真实的(实际上声音),好的(鼓励教会),和美丽的(阅读的乐趣). 他检查那些箱子。
传记重点 最有说服力的历史是通过人们而不是通过时间讲述的。 这解释了为什么“而不是历史的按时间顺序的百科全书版本”,DeYoung采取“一种传记方式”(6)。 我们得到有关伊雷纳厄斯、佩佩图亚和费利西蒂、阿塔纳修斯和扬·胡斯等人物的故事。 我们读到胡斯,作为一个牧师,胡斯是热情的,有时是热头.
他的布道也表现出幽默的幽默感.  . 与他这个年龄的大多数男人相比,他并不穷,但他也没有积累任何财富,也没有家庭庄园可以退休. 甚至在后来他的敌人指控他有许多过失和罪行时,他们从未指控他典型的祭司罪列表:醉酒,性不道德,懒惰,或奢侈.
(351) 当然,这种做法有缺点。 很多重要信息被忽略. 然而,DeYoung承认,“当作者讲述一个故事时,读者继续阅读的机会就更大了”(8)。 最有说服力的历史是通过人们讲述的。 历史往往不只是信息传递。
“讲述教会历史的目的——对大多数教会历史来说——是有意的启发,”DeYoung指出。 例如,“(Athanasius)希望第四世纪的基督徒能够得出不可回避的结论,即安东尼是一个英雄,他相信什么,他如何生活,对各地的基督追随者都有直接的教训”(71-72)。
从最早的几个世纪开始,基督徒就讲述了其他基督徒的故事. Polycarp对Foxe的《烈士书》的殉难经历, 近些年来,约翰·皮珀的短篇传记和斯蒂芬·尼科尔斯的《教会历史播客5分钟》唤醒了对非专业人士对过去更深入的研究的新赞赏。
当我们研究教会历史时, 我们的理论和解释并不停留在抽象中, 我们学习如何参与上帝挫败撒旦推翻教会的企图的伟大故事。
小说贡献 虽然已经存在一些对教会历史的扎实介绍,但是这首"人人教会历史"的第一卷填补了一个重要的位置. 几乎每名修习基督教历史的修道士,
这些作品为教室提供了40多年来教堂历史的标准介绍. 但我从未引导教会成员关注这些作品,
我们学习如何参与上帝挫败撒旦推翻教会的企图的伟大故事。 许多人想要的不只是事实和叙事。 因此我推荐布鲁斯·雪莱的教会史, 舍利写甚清净.
尼达姆精通地编织着教会历史的流派,具有洞察力和精准度. 但我在向教会成员推荐这些作品时仍会提出警告, 因为,尽管写作可能很简单, 内容是密集的, 充满了细微的, 历史的数据, 和名称索引, 能够延伸多页。
学校与修道院之间的隔阂令许多基督徒怀疑, DeYoung在写这本书时表现了杰出的纪律,作为一位受过训练的历史学家,他留下了许多脚注,叙事兔踪迹,以及神学辩论从最终产品中出来.
这本书之所以如此有用, 但DeYoung提供一条门路, 普通基督徒可以藉此学习探索主要来源, 我只希望凯西能读这本书;
本来可以帮助维持她前往天城的旅程
author: Travis Hearne

title: Help! My Bible Reading Feels Dead.
summary: Every passage takes its place in a larger drama. At the center of that drama stands a Person.
summary_zh: 她11年来每天早上都读她的圣经. 她的日记。 她通过她的通道祈祷. 她通过阅读计划、学习圣经和奉献指南而工作。
title_zh: 救命！我的读经生活毫无生气。
content: She has read her Bible every morning for 11 years. She journals. She prays through her passage. She has worked through reading plans , study Bibles, and devotional guides. And yet, sitting across from me in my study, she describes her Scripture reading with one word: dead. “I know I’m supposed to feel something,” she says. “But most days it just feels like going through the motions.” I’ve heard this confession more times than I can count from disciplined, sincere believers who do everything right and feel almost nothing. The standard prescriptions haven’t helped: Read more consistently, slow down and observe carefully, and find the application for your day. They’ve tried it all. The dryness remains. In most cases, the problem is a fundamentally misdirected reading method. Method We Were Handed Many of us were taught (implicitly or explicitly) to approach Scripture as primarily a collection of moral lessons, personal promises, and behavioral directives. We come to a passage asking, What am I supposed to do? What does God promise me here? How does this apply to my situation today? Scripture does instruct, promise, and call us to obey. But when this becomes our only lens, when we treat the Bible as a self-improvement manual with divine authority behind it, we’ve misread what kind of book it is. Moralistic Bible reading produces either pride when you keep up with the commands or despair when you cannot. Neither is an encounter with the living God . Moralistic Bible reading produces either pride when you keep up with the commands or despair when you cannot. Puritan writers such as Walter Marshall warned against what they broadly termed a “legal spirit”: treating God’s Word as a taskmaster instead of hearing in it the voice of a Father who acted in history to save a people for himself. Marshall’s classic Gospel Mystery of Sanctification remains the fullest treatment of this danger, and his diagnosis matches the wider Puritan tradition: The remedy was never more effort. It was a clearer sight of Christ. Road to Emmaus Changes Everything On the afternoon of the first Easter, two disciples walked from Jerusalem to Emmaus with shattered hopes and a Scripture they thought they understood. Then a stranger joined them on the road. “And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself” (Luke 24:27). Jesus didn’t give them a new application strategy. He gave them a new reading of the same Scripture they already possessed. Moses, the Prophets, the Psalms—all of it spoke of him. The entire redemptive history of Israel was moving toward him, finding its meaning in him, and flowing from him. The result wasn’t intellectual satisfaction but a burning heart. “Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us on the road, while he opened to us the Scriptures?” (v. 32). This “burning” is what theologians call the fruit of redemptive-historical reading. When you read Scripture as God’s unfolding story of redemption , traced through creation, fall, promise, covenant, fulfillment, and consummation, every passage takes its place in a larger drama. At the center of that drama stands a Person. You’re being introduced, again and again, to him. Read the Whole Story Consider what this lens opens up in familiar passages. Leviticus’s sacrificial system, which modern readers so often experience as tedious, becomes luminous when read as the redemptive-historical preparation for the once-for-all sacrifice of the Lamb of God. Every slaughtered animal announces the same truth: Something must die; sin requires atonement; a substitute must bear what the guilty cannot. You arrive at Calvary, and the whole system resolves into its intended meaning. Every passage takes its place in a larger drama. At the center of that drama stands a Person. The psalms of lament, those raw and disorienting cries of abandonment, take on new weight when you see that the Son of God himself prayed them from the cross. “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” (Ps. 22:1) isn’t only David’s prayer and your prayer; it’s Christ’s prayer, offered as a model for every broken human being who has ever felt forsaken (Matt. 27:46). You’re praying with your great High Priest. All the Scriptures concern him. That gravity, once felt, pulls everything into focus. Three Questions Careful reading, observation, and application remain essential. What changes is the frame those practices work within. Before asking what you should do, consider these three questions of your passage: 1. Where is this passage in the story of redemption? Is this text in the period of promise, covenant, or fulfillment? What was God doing here in the history of salvation? 2. How does this passage point toward or flow from the work of Christ? Every text exists within a story that culminates in him. 3. What does this reveal about the God who gave his Son? Scripture’s deepest purpose is the knowledge of God , and his fullest disclosure is the crucified and risen Son. These questions give application its proper weight. When you see what God has done in Christ, obedience becomes response instead of performance. You’re not working to earn anything. You’re responding to everything already given. Your Heart Can Still Burn My church member didn’t have a discipline problem. She had more discipline than most. She had been reading a love letter as an instruction manual, and instruction manuals don’t make hearts burn. The remedy for devotional dryness is learning to read Scripture the way its Author intended, as a unified, Christ-centered story of redemption, alive in every part, burning toward a consummation that has already broken into history on Easter morning. The stranger on the road to Emmaus is still opening the Scriptures. The question is whether we read them in a way that positions us to recognize him when he does.
content_zh:
她11年来每天早上都读她的圣经. 她的日记。 她通过她的通道祈祷. 她通过阅读计划、学习圣经和奉献指南而工作。 然而,坐在我书房的对面, 她用一个词描述她的圣经阅读: 死亡。 “我知道我应该感觉到什么,”她说。
“但大多数时候, 我听到这种忏悔的次数比我能数的多, 标准处方没有帮助:更一致地阅读、减慢和仔细观察, 他们都试过了。 干燥犹存.
在大多数情况下,问题是一个根本错误的阅读方法. 许多人(隐含或明确)被教导将《圣经》视为主要道德教训、个人承诺和行为指令的集合。 我们来到一个段落 问,我该怎么办? 上帝答应我什么? 这对我今天的处境有何影响?
圣经的确教导我们,答应我们,叫我们服从。 但当这成为我们唯一的镜头时, 当我们把《圣经》当作一本有神圣权威的自我改进手册, 道德主义 圣经的阅读要么在遵守命令时产生自豪感,要么在做不到的情况下产生绝望感. 也没有遇到活神。
道德主义 圣经的阅读要么在遵守命令时产生自豪感,要么在做不到的情况下产生绝望感. 例如沃尔特·马歇尔(Walter Marshall)这样的清教徒作家警告说,
马歇尔经典的福音圣洁神秘论仍然是最充分地处理这种危险,他的诊断符合更广泛的清教徒传统: 补救办法从未如此努力。 更清楚地看到基督。
通往艾玛乌斯的路改变一切 在第一个复活节的下午,两个门徒带着破碎的希望和他们认为能理解的经典从耶路撒冷走到艾玛乌斯. 然后一个陌生人在路上加入了他们 他从穆萨和众先知开始,在一切天经中,他都要对他们解释自己所受的刑罚。
耶稣没有给他们新的应用策略。 他使他们重新诵读他们所有的经典。 穆萨、众先知、众菩萨,都曾提到他。 以色列的整个红色历史都朝他走去,从他那里找到它的意义。 其结果不是智力满意,
“当他在路上和我们说话的时候,难道我们的心没有烧着吗?” 这种“燃烧”是神学家所说的红发-历史读物的果实。 当你把《圣经》读成上帝的救赎故事时, 每段故事都以更大的戏剧形式出现。
剧情的核心是人物 你不断被介绍给他。 阅读"全史话" 考虑这个镜头在熟悉的段落中打开什么. 利维提库斯的牺牲制度,现代读者经常以乏味的眼光体验,在读作红色的先发制人-历史的准备,一劳永逸地牺牲上帝的羔羊时,这种制度就变得光辉了。
每个被屠宰的动物都宣告同样的真理:某事必须死;罪恶需要赎罪;替代者必须承担有罪者所不能承担的. 你到达卡尔瓦里,整个系统 解决它的意图。 每一个段落都在更大的戏剧中占据其位置. 剧情的核心是人物
哀叹的诗歌, 那些生动的和令人不快的关于抛弃的呼声, 承担了新的重量 当你看到上帝之子自己 从十字架上祈祷。 “我的上帝,我的上帝,你为什么抛弃我?”(P.22:1)不仅仅是大卫的祷告和你的祷告;而是基督的祷告,作为每一个曾经感觉被抛弃的破碎人类的典范(Matt. 27:46)。
你正在和你的大祭司祈祷。 所有经典都与他有关。 引力一旦被感觉到 就会把一切都引向焦点 三个问题仍然至关重要。 改变之处是这些做法在其中发挥作用。 在问起你该做什么之前,考虑一下你通过的三个问题: 1.赎罪故事中的这个段落在哪里?
这是在承诺、盟约或实现的时期吗? 救赎史上上帝在这里做什么? 2. 这一段落如何指向或来自基督的工作? 每一条文字都存在于一个故事里,而故事的结局就是他. 3. 这揭示了给儿子的神是什么?
《圣经》最深的旨意是了解上帝,他最充分地揭示了被钉死在十字架上的儿子。 这些问题给予适当重视。 当你看到上帝在基督中所做的,服从变成了回应而不是表现. 你的工作不是赚钱。 你正在回应已经给出的一切。
你的心还能燃烧 我的教会成员没有纪律问题。 她的纪律比大多数人都强 她读过一封情书,
对奉献性干燥的补救是学习如何阅读《圣经》,其作者的意图是,作为一个统一的、以基督为中心的救赎故事,在每一部分都是活的,在复活节早晨已经破解历史。 前往艾玛乌斯路上的陌生人仍在打开"圣经".
问题是,我们是否在阅读这些内容时,能够使我们在认识他时认出他。
author: Kim Dang

title: 5 Reasons Why It’s Hard to Discuss Our AI Fears
summary: Christians aren’t remotely ready for the age of AI. Learn more about it and be ready to draw the line.
summary_zh: 从Jensen Huang离开Nvidia(和在Nvidia恢复)的报导、大型技术公司的连锁失败, 最近的对话使我得出了一个令人不快的结论:大多数基督徒还没有为AI时代做好准备。 这里有五个复杂因素,使得谈论AI变得困难. 1. AI不是单一的;
title_zh: 难以讨论我们对人工智能的恐惧的5个原因
content: Between the coverage of Jensen Huang’s departure from (and reinstatement at) Nvidia , the cascading failures in large tech companies , and the obvious cracks in critical infrastructure , many people are feeling acute uncertainty about technology . Recent conversations have led me to an uncomfortable conclusion: Most Christians aren’t remotely ready for the era of AI. Here are five complexities that make talking about AI difficult. 1. AI is not monolithic; it is a series of overlapping epochs. The first epoch of AI is the LLM stage (2022–present). This epoch began with the release of ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and other models. The second epoch is the agentic AI stage that began this year. The epoch marks the introduction of AI bots such as OpenClaw, Grok Bot, and Muse. The third epoch, which hasn’t arrived yet but will likely begin in 2027 or 2028, is the physical AI stage. The beginning of this epoch will be marked by the arrival of robots (think Tesla’s Optimus robot) that use AI to replicate human actions in the wider world. As I have written elsewhere , these epochs will move and change at speeds faster than we can understand. 2. A wise posture toward AI looks different for four groups of Christians. These four groups (more could be added) are parents, pastors and ministry leaders, educators, and marketplace leaders. Each of these groups needs better education on AI. And after they have been educated, some groups may need to use AI more, and some need to use it less. Parents need to learn from the social media era and better protect their kids. We’ve seen how Gen Z was wrecked by social media apps. We can prevent a similar level of harm to Gen Alpha by making sure they’re not overexposed to AI while they’re young. Pastors and ministry leaders need to learn to develop greater discernment toward AI besides “I love it” or “I hate it.” The “I hate it” group needs to recognize legitimate uses for AI, especially in administrative, systematic, and process situations. The “I love it” group needs to know the serious dangers around cognitive off-loading, intellectual and spiritual malformation when using AI for sermon prep, and legal issues surrounding data. Educators, teachers, and administrators—especially those in Christian education contexts—need to better understand the technology and its neurobiological implications on young people. AI skills aren’t hard to acquire. Learning about harnesses, prompt engineering, MCPs, and markdown files on YouTube can take you from zero to 100 in a matter of hours. These tools don’t need to be incorporated in every grade or every subject. The biggest needs in Christian education should be spiritual formation, the cultivation of virtue, the discipline of reading books and long-form media, and the ability to craft analogy arguments that can be defended orally and in writing. For marketplace leaders, they need to know it’s reasonable to use AI for certain things and then not want it anywhere near other parts of your day. That is, admittedly, a difficult tension to hold. Many of us are in more than one of these four groups. It will take a great amount of wisdom to parse how to walk in wisdom with AI at our company and under the roof of our home. We need to learn how to appreciate the tech and how we can use it in one domain while insisting it not seep into another domain. It’s OK to want AI to make breakthroughs in medicine and to not want it break the intellectual supply chain of your pastor’s sermon prep. 3. We’re undereducated and overconfident about the tool we’re using all the time. The average person’s education levels about AI are uncomfortably low. This means low understanding on how this technology works, what it’s good at, what it struggles with, what we should use it for, what we shouldn’t use it for, and how to best use it. It’s OK to want AI to make breakthroughs in medicine and to not want it break the intellectual supply chain of your pastor’s sermon prep. At the same time, many people believe they know what they’re doing when they use AI. They put a prompt in and get a lengthy response back, so they assume they’re doing something right. But that is a naive approach. In reality, many Christians are on the Dunning-Kruger curve at the peak of “Mount Stupid” where they think they have a solid grasp of AI and yet they know next to nothing. I have recently been at a few different universities interacting with students, campus ministers, faculty, and administration. It has been illuminating. Departments fall all over the place terms of how they are thinking about AI. Departments who hate it probably need more understanding, and the folks who love it probably need more discernment. Anecdotally, I find the undereducation/overconfidence paradox at work among the students I’ve interacted with. When I polled several hundred students across multiple universities and departments, 80 percent of the students said they use AI daily. But when I followed up and asked them whether they knew what an AI harness was, what a markdown file was, or if they had heard the term “prompt engineering,” only one hand went up. Despite their lack of knowledge about AI, the students tend to show a lot more concern about AI than their professors do. Conversations I’ve had with faculty and administration weren’t much better; in many conversations, I found their ignorance of and confidence in AI more deeply concerning than their students’. I’ve heard administrators commend the use of AI for free cognitive behavioral therapy and for things even cringier than that. These are serious Christians with advanced degrees! It’s a huge problem. That’s why The Gospel Coalition has published a benchmark to show you what AI models do well regarding religious questions and where you should run in the other direction. 4. AI will forever change how humans acquire knowledge. As far back as humans remember, knowledge has transferred from one human mind to another through either embodied teaching or text. AI destroys that direct human-mind to human-mind chain and inserts itself as a middleman. This makes AI a kind of high priest of knowledge and creates an “ intellectual Strait of Hormuz .” 5. Everyone needs proactive rules about what they will and will not use AI for. Almost nobody that I interact with has developed proactive rules for when he or she does and doesn’t use AI. This is a big problem. Every new use case must have intellectual and spiritual justification before we adopt it. One such example for me is that I never use AI for wisdom. Knowledge, sometimes . Wisdom, never . Wisdom is for prayer, the Bible, books, and trusted advice from people. Drawing a line and sticking to it is essential. Way Forward On the one hand, I’m not surprised that Christians are behind the curve on AI. As the writers laid out in TGC’s new book The AI Apocalypse , this technology has both incredible opportunities and tremendous dangers. The news cycle related to Nvidia alone this week is impossibly fast to keep up with. To address this education gap I’m working with TGC’s women’s team to host a four-week, online interactive cohort on biblical wisdom for AI, starting in January. Every new use case must have intellectual and spiritual justification before adoption. On the other hand, I’m witnessing both uncritical adoption and unhelpful rejection among many Christians. If I were to prescribe a better way forward, I suggest three things. 1. Christians need to understand that AI isn’t one thing. In some use cases, AI extends common grace. In other use cases, AI is truly horrible. We should have the discernment to see both. 2. Christians should better educate themselves on how AI technology works, what it’s good at, where it struggles, and what we should and shouldn’t use it for. 3. Christians should draft clear, proactive rules rooted in a Christian worldview on when they will and won’t use AI and why.
content_zh:
从Jensen Huang离开Nvidia(和在Nvidia恢复)的报导、大型技术公司的连锁失败, 最近的对话使我得出了一个令人不快的结论:大多数基督徒还没有为AI时代做好准备。
这里有五个复杂因素,使得谈论AI变得困难. 1. AI不是单一的;它是一系列重叠的时代。 AI的第一个时代是LLM阶段(2022年–现在). 这个时代始于ChatGPT,克劳德,双子座等模型的发布. 第二个时代是今年开始的代理AI阶段.
这个时代标志着AI bot的引入,如OpenClaw,Grok Bot,和Muse. 第三个时代是物理AI阶段, 这个时代的开始将标志着机器人(Tesla's Optimus robot)的到来,他们利用AI在更广泛的世界中复制人类行动.
正如我在别处所写的那样,这些时代将以我们无法理解的速度移动和改变。 2. 四个基督徒群体对AI的明智姿态不同。 这四个团体(还可以增加)是父母、牧师和部委领导人、教育工作者和市场领导人。 每个群体都需要更好的AI教育.
而在他们受过教育后,有些群体可能需要多使用AI,有些则需要少使用. 父母需要从社交媒体时代学习,更好地保护孩子. Gen Z如何被社交媒体应用破坏。 透过确保年轻时不会过度接触AI,
除了“我爱它”或“我讨厌它 ” , 牧师和部委领导人需要学会对AI产生更大的认知。 “我恨它”团体需要承认对大赦国际的合法使用,特别是在行政、系统和程序方面。
“我爱它”团体在使用AI进行布道准备时需要了解认知卸载、智力和精神畸形以及围绕数据的法律问题等严重危险。 教育工作者、教师和行政人员,特别是基督教教育背景的人员,需要更好地了解技术及其对年轻人的神经生物影响。

诚然,这是难以维持的紧张局势。 我们许多人属于这四组人中不止一组人。 要在公司和我们家的屋檐下 与AI一起智慧地走下去,需要极大的智慧。 我们需要学习如何欣赏技术,以及如何在一个领域使用技术,同时坚持技术不能渗入另一个领域。
希望AI在医学上取得突破, 3. 我们的教育不足,对于我们一直使用的工具过于自信。 有关人工智能的平均教育水平低得令人不快。
这意味着对于这种技术如何运作、它擅长什么、它与什么斗争、我们应该如何使用它、我们不应该使用它,以及如何最好地使用它缺乏了解。 希望AI在医学上取得突破,

最近,我在几所不同的大学与学生、校园部长、教职员工和行政人员互动。 它一直在发光。 各部门对AI的思考遍及各地。 讨厌它的部门可能需要更多的理解,喜欢它的人可能需要更多的辨识.
我发现与我互动的学生工作时, 当我在多个大学和部门调查数百名学生时,80%的学生说他们每天使用AI。
但当我跟踪问他们是否知道AI系系, 尽管学生们对AI缺乏了解,但往往比他们的教授对AI表现出更多的关注. 我与教职员工和行政人员的谈话并不更好。
在很多对话中,我发现他们对大赦国际的无知和信心比他们的学生更深厚。 我听到管理者赞扬使用AI免费认知行为疗法, 他们是有高级学位的基督徒! 这是一个巨大的问题。
因此福音联盟公布了一个基准, 以显示AI模型在宗教问题上做得好, 4. 大赦国际将永远改变人类获得知识的方式。 早在人类记忆中,知识就已经通过隐含的教学或文字从一个人类的思想转移到另一个人的思想.
AI摧毁了那些将人心引向人心的链条,并插入自己作为中间人. 这让大赦国际成为知识的大祭司,并创造了“知识型霍尔木兹海峡 ” 。 每个人都需要主动的规则 关于他们愿意和不会使用AI。 与我互动的几乎没有人会制定主动的规则, 这是一个大问题。
每一个新的使用案例,在我们通过之前,都必须有理智和精神上的理由. 对我来说,一个这样的例子是,我从来没有用AI来表达智慧. 知识,有时。 智慧,永远不要。 智慧是用于祈祷,圣经,书籍,以及人们信任的建议. 划一条线,坚持下去至关重要。 前进之路 我并不感到惊讶,
正如TGC新书《启示录》中阐述的, 本周仅与Nvidia有关的新闻周期无法跟上。 为了弥补这一教育差距,我正在与TGC的妇女团队合作,从1月开始为AI主办为期四周的在线互动小组,介绍圣经智慧。
每一个新的使用案例在通过前都必须有智力和精神上的理由。 我亲眼目睹许多基督教徒毫无批评的领养, 如果我要规定更好的前进方向,我建议做三件事。 基督徒需要明白, 在某些情况下,大赦国际给予共同恩惠。
在其他使用情况下,AI的确很可怕. 我们应该有辨别力来看到两者。 2. 基督徒应该更好地教育自己AI技术如何运作,它擅长什么,它在哪里挣扎,以及我们应该和不应该用来什么。 3. 基督徒应起草明确、积极主动的规则,这些规则植根于基督教的世界观中,关于他们何时会使用和不会使用人工智能以及为什么。

title: How to Preach to Workers
summary: The New Testament offers two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching.
summary_zh: 我还记得我第一次听到关于上帝设计工作的布道。 科林·史密斯牧师在"十诫"系列中工作, 我希望听到关于休息的富有挑战性的话。 他上半场讲道工作时,我感到惊讶。 由于他是一个优秀的传教士,史密斯提醒我们注意我们可能忽略的那段话:"六天你必须努力,并做你所有的工作.
title_zh: 如何向工人传福音
content: I still remember the first time I heard a sermon on God’s design for work. Pastor Colin Smith was in a series working through the Ten Commandments, and he’d come to the fourth command about the Sabbath. I was expecting to hear challenging words about rest. So I was surprised when he spent the first half of his sermon talking about work. Because he’s a good exegetical preacher, Smith reminded us to pay attention to the part of the passage we might overlook: “Six days you shall labor, and do all your work . . .” (Ex. 20:9). For 16 minutes, Smith preached about God’s design for work. He explained how God modeled work in creation, crafting and making our world like a builder, engineer, and artist. And since humans were created in the likeness of this God, our labors are a significant part of what it means to represent him in the world. Then he started naming regular kinds of work—such as the school crossing guard who creates a zone of safety and protection for children. He shared example after example, even naming those who are were unemployed and looking for work as engaging in a form of dignified labor. They can please God as they trust him to provide and remain diligent to seek out what’s next. At the time, I was working a summer landscaping job between semesters at seminary. I took the job because it was necessary, not because I found it personally fulfilling or spiritually significant. I’d been subconsciously wanting to be done with mowing lawns and picking weeds so I could get back to the important work of studying Scripture. But God used Smith’s sermon to reorient my ordinary labor. Preaching with workers in mind is vital to shepherding a congregation. It reminds church members that work is a primary context for discipleship and helps them work out the implications of God’s Word where they spend a large portion of their time. The New Testament gives two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching. Work as an Illustration of the Kingdom As the eternal, perfect Son of God, Jesus isn’t only Savior and Lord but also the most brilliant teacher the world has ever heard. Therefore, as preachers, we take his pedagogy seriously even as we learn his precepts and mimic his practices. Jesus often proclaims the good news by igniting people’s imaginations and explaining eternal truths in concrete realities, including the body (Matt. 6:22; 7:3–5; 24:7–8), nature (Matt. 6:28–29; Mark 11:23; Luke 17:6), and food (Matt. 13:33; John 6:35, 53–56). But Jesus’s most consistent metaphor for the truths of the kingdom is work and workers. Klaus Issler’s survey reveals that of the 37 parables in the Synoptic Gospels, 32 reference work or workers, representing 22 different work roles. In 25 of the parables, work is a main part of the storyline. Here are examples: The farmer sows the seed (Matt. 13). The faithful manager gives the servants of the household food at the proper time (Luke 12:42). Even an unjust judge will give a persistent widow justice (18:1–8). The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). A king going into battle should take counsel to see if he’s strong enough before he a ttacks (Luke 14:31). When Jesus describes what it meant to follow him and live in his kingdom, why does he use the ordinary language of work and workers? First, God’s self-disclosure is often wrapped in the language of work. For instance, he’s portrayed as a composer and performer (Deut. 31:19), a tentmaker (Job 9:8), a garment maker and dresser (29:14), a shepherd (Ps. 23:1–4), a builder (Prov. 8:27–31), a metalworker (Isa. 1:24–26), a potter (31:9), and a farmer (Hos. 10:11). If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. Second, Jesus likely spent nearly six times as many years as a regular worker than he did in his public ministry—probably as a stonemason, either running a small family business or working as a day laborer. Wouldn’t it make sense that 17 or 18 years of regular work would inform the language of his teaching? It isn’t a coincidence that Jesus summarizes the implications of his teaching with the image of two builders: one who built on a sturdy foundation and one who built on sand (Matt. 7:24–27). Jesus knows by experience the ramifications of choosing the wrong foundation. So that’s the mental model he gives us to understand ways we can respond to his teaching. From Jesus to the Pulpit Jesus isn’t alone in using work as an illustration of the kingdom. Paul calls himself an expert builder who lays a foundation others build on (1 Cor. 3:10). He also instructs Timothy to meditate on the work of soldiers, athletes, and farmers to learn what it means to be a faithful pastor in Ephesus (2 Tim. 2:3–7). James too, in his final climactic call to wait for the Lord’s return, tells us to consider farmers who patiently wait for autumn and spring rains (James 5:7–8). When the New Testament writers explain what it means to walk with God, they regularly use examples from ordinary work. What might this mean for preachers today? As we explain the principles of God’s kingdom, how could we illustrate gospel truths with the work of baristas, software developers, accountants, realtors, or construction workers? How are God’s ways like a home inspector or a pilot? How is following him like the work of a middle manager or a plumber? To teach like Jesus and the writers of the epistles is to search out and proclaim the truth of the kingdom in the language of regular work. Along with making our teaching vivid, this dignifies people—in a unique way, their daily work is a picture of how God is at work in the world, and we can better understand who he is and what he calls us to if we look closely at the labor of his image-bearers. Work as an Application of the Gospel While Jesus primarily uses work to illustrate the kingdom, other New Testament writers mention work as a direct application of embracing the gospel. And even though the epistles aren’t sermons, they demonstrate how the apostles applied the gospel to common pastoral and contextual issues. For instance, Paul encourages the Corinthians, who have just been told of the wonders of the resurrection body, to know that their labor in the Lord isn’t in vain (1 Cor. 15:58). In a culture of persistent stealing, the Ephesians are called to do work that produces something good, so they’ll be able to give to those in need (Eph. 4:28). Bondservants with little power or agency are told to work diligently (6:5–9), knowing they’ll receive an inheritance as their reward and that their true Master is God himself (Col. 3:23–24). Those in Thessalonica who deem it more spiritual to constantly await God’s return without worrying about ordinary work are commanded to lead quiet lives, working with their hands (1 Thess. 4:11–12). James confronts boastful business leaders, saying they need to have a more God-dependent outlook (James 4:13–16) and that rich landowners who aren’t paying their workers can expect judgment (5:1–6). And Paul calls Philemon to envision a new working relationship with Onesimus, based not on power or status but on brotherly love and affection (Philem. 1:10–16). After articulating the gospel, the epistle writers consistently model that its application must be made clearly and contextually to people’s work. This suggests work should be a top-tier pastoral concern, with implications for the church’s regular teaching ministry. Work should be a top-tier pastoral concern, with implications for the church’s regular teaching ministry. Preaching to workers is a lifelong endeavor. Modeled by Jesus, the New Testament authors, and countless preachers throughout church history, in many times and in many places, the practice is rooted in pastoral curiosity and a desire to shepherd the people of God in their ordinary lives. 我还记得我第一次听到关于上帝设计工作的布道。 科林·史密斯牧师在"十诫"系列中工作, 我希望听到关于休息的富有挑战性的话。 他上半场讲道工作时,我感到惊讶。
由于他是一个优秀的传教士,史密斯提醒我们注意我们可能忽略的那段话:"六天你必须努力,并做你所有的工作."(ex.20:9). 16分钟,史密斯宣扬上帝的工作设计. 他解释了上帝如何塑造我们的世界 像一个建筑师、工程师和艺术家
由于人类是在这个神的像中创造出来的, 我们的劳动是世界上代表他的意义的重要部分. 然后,他开始点名从事常规工作,例如学校越野警卫,为儿童创造一个安全和保护的地区。
他举了个例子,甚至将那些失业和寻找工作的人命名为从事一种有尊严的劳动。 他们可以取悦上帝, 因为他们相信上帝提供, 当时我在神学院的暑期园林设计工作
我接受这份工作是因为有必要,而不是因为我发现这份工作是个人的满足或精神意义。 我潜意识地想要完成割草和摘草, 但上帝用史密斯的布道来调整我的普通劳动。 向工人宣讲对牧羊人至关重要。
它提醒教会成员,工作是门徒活动的主要背景,帮助他们解决神话的影响,在那里他们花费了大量的时间. "新约"为传教士如何在教学中考虑工人给出了两种范式.
发挥王国的作用 耶稣不仅是救世主, 因此,作为传教士,我们在学习他的戒律和模仿他的做法时,也认真对待他的教学方法.
耶稣经常通过点燃人们的想象力和在具体现实中解释永恒的真理来宣告好消息,包括身体(Matt. 6:22;7:3–5;24:7–8),自然(Matt. 6:28–29;Mark 11:23;Luke 17:6)和食物(Matt. 13:33;John 6:35,53–56). 但耶稣对王国真理最一致的比喻是工作和工人.
Klaus Issler的调查显示,在Synoptic福音书中的37个比喻中,有32个参考工作或工人,代表了22个不同的工作角色. 在25个比喻中,作品是故事情节的主要部分. 以下是例子:农民播种(Matt.13). 忠诚的经理在适当的时候给家庭食物的仆人(公爵12:42).
即使是不公正的法官也会给守寡者以持续的公正(18:1-8). 善牧者为羊舍命(约翰10:11). 一个参战的国王应该接受建议, 当耶稣描述追随他并生活在他的王国的意义时,他为什么使用普通的劳动和工人语言?
首先,上帝的自我披露往往用工作语言包扎。 例如,他被描绘成作曲家和表演者(德国31:19)、帐篷匠(约旦9:8)、制衣师和梳妆师(29:14)、牧羊人(Ps.23:1-4)、建筑师(Prov.8:27-31)、金属工人(Isa:1:24-26)、锅炉工(31:9)和农民(Hos:10:11)。
如果上帝是最初的工人,那么整个工作领域可以教我们他的方法是有意义的. 如果上帝是最初的工人,那么整个工作领域可以教我们他的方法是有意义的.
第二,耶稣作为一名普通工人可能花费了将近六倍于他在公共部委所花费的时间——可能是做石匠,或者经营一家小家庭企业,或者做日工。 17年或18年的正常工作会影响他教学的语言,
耶稣用两个建筑师的形象来总结其教学的意义, 耶稣通过经验知道选择错误的基础的后果. 所以这就是他给我们的心理模型 来理解我们如何回应他的教导。
从耶稣到雕塑耶稣, 保罗自称是一位专家建筑师,他为他人的建设奠定了基础(1 Cor. 3:10). 他还指示蒂莫西沉思士兵,运动员,农民的工作,学习在以弗所做忠实牧师的意义(2 Tim.2:3-7).
詹姆斯在最后的气候呼吁中也要求我们等待主的归来,告诉我们考虑耐心等待秋天和春雨的农民(詹姆斯5:7–8). 新约作家在解释与神同行的意义时,经常使用普通作品中的例子. 这对今天的传教士意味着什么?
当我们解释上帝王国的原则时,我们如何用律师、软件开发者、会计师、房地产商或建筑工人的工作来说明福音真理呢? 上帝如何像一个家庭巡视员或飞行员? 如何跟随他 像一个中层经理或水管工的工作?
像耶稣和史诗的作家一样教书,就是用正规作品的语言去探寻和宣告王国的真理. 除了生动的教学之外,这使我们深受人尊敬——以独特的方式,他们的日常工作是描绘上帝如何在世界上工作,如果我们仔细观察他的形象持有者的工作,我们就能更好地了解他是谁,以及他对我们的称呼。
虽然耶稣主要利用作品来说明王国,但其他新约作家提到作品是接受福音的直接应用. 也说明使徒们如何将福音运用到共同的牧业和背景问题上。
例如,保罗鼓励刚刚被告知复活神体奇迹的科林斯人知道他们在主的劳动并非徒劳(第15:58节)。 在持续偷窃的文化中, 以弗所人被要求做一些能产生好东西的工作,
他们知道自己将获得遗产作为报酬, 并且他们真正的主人是上帝(Col. 3:23-24)。 在Thessalonica,那些认为在不担心普通工作的情况下不断等待上帝的归来更具有精神的人,被命令过着平静的生活,用双手工作(1 Thess. 4:11–12).
James面对自夸的商业领袖,说他们需要有一个更依赖上帝的前景(James 4:13–16),而那些不支付工人工资的富有地主可以期待判断(5:1–6)。 保罗呼吁菲勒蒙设想与Onesimus建立新的工作关系,这种关系不是基于权力或地位,而是基于兄弟般的爱和亲情(Philem. 1:10-16).

title: The Gospel Coalition 2026 Book Awards
summary: The Gospel Coalition selects the best Christian books published in 2026 in our annual TGC Book Awards.
